noveltyJustification: Hooks and workflow path filters expose commit-time ordering constraints, auto-writing validators and CI blind spots for a new .skilled source root.
keyQuestions: Which repository gates, CI workflows, documentation and external references become blockers?
Which migration mechanics create ordering constraints or irrecoverable breakage?
answeredQuestions: Pre-commit, pre-push, hook installation, .gitignore and representative CI path filters all hardcode .opencode and require coordinated contract updates.

ruledOut.approach: Update only GitHub Actions commands after the move
ruledOut.reason: Installed local hooks and pre-push gates resolve .opencode before CI runs and can block or silently skip the migration commit.

keyFindings.finding: Pre-commit uses .opencode hook, checker, mirror, route-remint and metadata paths.
Pre-push classifies and validates skill/routing changes through .opencode paths.
Workflow path filters and job commands enumerate .opencode trees and can miss .skilled-only changes.
